- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after peak), model often fails to correct; apply “reversion bias” rule: if forecast > true outcome by >5%, reduce by 2–5% in next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use “sentiment lag” rule: if sentiment changes direction within 5 days, adjust forecast 1–3 days later to match sentiment trend.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% if sentiment remains flat for 3+ days.
